text:
Ajay: FYI seeing a 2.6x increase in prefix cache miss rate for /v1/chat generate on long sessions after the kernel selection roll yesterday. Spike is concentrated on structured-output prompts (tables / JSON). attaching perf traces and hit-rate CSV.

Lina: can you paste the numbers? global vs per-customer?

Ajay: Global prefix hit-rate went from 78% -> 54% for sessions >8k tokens. For RAG+chat subset it's ~41%. Median p50 latency +18ms, p95 +60ms.

Matt: That aligns with my kernel swap deploy at 03:20UTC (changed attention kernel for int8 seq_len >1024). Did the cache key schema change too?

Nina: We also tweaked batching heuristics yesterday to favor larger microbatches when seq_len distribution skewed; could affect warmup behaviour and KV cache priming.

Ajay: Keying hasn't intentionally changed, but a normalization tweak landed that includes role markers now. Snippet: 
```
def make_cache_key(prefix_tokens):
    # previously stripped role markers
    norm = normalize(prefix_tokens, keep_roles=True)
    return sha1(norm)
```
This made many previously-colliding prefixes distinct -> drop in reuse.

Matt: Oof. That explains a lot. Any quick rollback option?

Lina: Two near-term mitigations: 1) revert role inclusion in normalization; 2) warmstart popular conversation prefixes into the pod cache during startup (we already have top-K per-customer stats).

Ajay: Canary: warmstart top-5k prefixes reduced miss-rate by ~12% within first 5 minutes but memory usage increased ~8%. Warmstart plus TTL trimming helps.

Nina: For long-context chats we should consider truncation policy for keying: e.g., keep last 1024 tokens for key creation so repeated endings match even if earlier system prompts differ.

Matt: Also prototype approximate keying (LSH / simhash) for really high-cardinality prefix space — trades false positives for higher effective hit-rate.

perf-bot: perf/regression alert #1769991234 linked: https://perf/reports/1769991234 :thinking:

Ajay: Action items: (a) revert normalization change in next patch and run canary; (b) launch warmstart job for top prefixes per-region with TTL; (c) run LSH prototype on sampled workload; (d) instrument KV lookup + kernel path to measure miss penalty. I'll draft the revert PR.

Lina: I'll own the warmstart job and add adaptive TTLs (short TTL for preloads, longer for live fills).

Nina: I'll add tracing around kernel selection -> kv lookup -> decode to see if new kernel increases p95 on misses. Need microprofile traces.

Matt: Ping me for PR review. +1 for revert asap. :thumbsup:

Ajay: uploaded perf attach: s3://perf/1769991234/trace.zip
